result.title: Ref-YOLO-World: Decoupling Text-Side Computation for Efficient Referring Expression Comprehension on Edge Devices
result.summary: Many high-accuracy referring expression comprehension (REC) methods produce image-dependent multimodal representations. These representations must be recomputed for every video frame, even when the referring expression remains unchanged. Fast open-vocabulary detectors such as YOLO-World instead pre-encode text once and reuse it throughout the stream. However, encoding each referring expression as a single embedding prevents explicit token-level correspondence. We propose Ref-YOLO-World, which separates text-side computation that depends only on the referring expression from image processing and reuses its outputs across frames. Two lightweight modules inject cached per-token text features into YOLO-World's detection path. Ref-YOLO-World achieves 81.29% Acc@0.5 on RefCOCOg val, the highest among REC models with a decoupled text branch, and consistently outperforms a fine-tuned YOLO-World. Precomputation reduces per-image inference time by 18.5%, yielding 47.0 FPS. A Core ML version runs at 15.73 FPS on an iPhone 15 Pro, demonstrating efficient on-device REC. Code is available at https://github.com/sakusaku3939/Ref-YOLO-World.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Ref-YOLO-World，把仅依赖指代表达的文本侧计算与图像处理解耦，缓存 per-token 文本特征并跨帧复用，用于边缘设备上的指代表达理解。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作属检测器工程优化，核心是文本编码缓存与加速，未涉及 latent 推理状态、证据获取或停止决策，仅「缓存复用」字样与关注点表面相似，缺少可供核查的实质借鉴线索。
